ROLE: Handle a peer read shutdown: first process every complete packet still buffered (so a final PUBLISH is still routed), then discard any partial tail and put the session into CLOSING so already queued output is flushed before the descriptor is closed.

STRUCT.NAME: struct broker
STRUCT.ROLE: registry used by the framing step

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: connection whose buffered frames are handled and which then drains its queue

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: receive buffer whose partial tail is discarded; output queue is left intact

FUNC.NAME: session_state
FUNC.ROLE: decide whether frames may still be processed and whether the session is already CLOSED/CLOSING

FUNC.NAME: session_input
FUNC.ROLE: borrow the receive buffer to discard the trailing partial bytes

FUNC.NAME: buffer_consume
FUNC.ROLE: drop the partial tail (len bytes) while keeping the storage

FUNC.NAME: session_close_after_flush
FUNC.ROLE: enter CLOSING with the queued output preserved

FUNC.NAME: broker_process_input
FUNC.ROLE: same-file: handle every complete buffered frame

VAR.NAME: SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT
VAR.ROLE: state in which buffered bytes are still framed (a CONNECT may be pending)

VAR.NAME: SESSION_READY
VAR.ROLE: state in which buffered bytes are still framed

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSING
VAR.ROLE: state that already preserves the queue and must not be overwritten

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: buffer_consume
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; n bytes are removed from the front (n > len is clamped) and the storage is kept
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: storage stays with the receive buffer; discarding a partial frame releases nothing
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; buffer_consume(in, in->len) empties the receive buffer with its capacity intact

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_close_after_flush
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: void; READY or AWAITING_CONNECT becomes CLOSING with the queued output preserved; a session that is already CLOSING or CLOSED is unchanged
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: keeps the session owning its descriptor and queued bytes; the descriptor is closed later by the writer path or broker_reap once the queue is empty

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_state
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the current lifecycle state; SESSION_CLOSED for NULL

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: session_input
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: borrowed receive buffer, NULL only for a NULL session
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; the session keeps the storage

LOGIC.INPUT: b: broker registry. s: the session whose peer shut down its write side or whose read failed; s is still registered and owns its descriptor and buffers.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If s is NULL return. 2. st = session_state(s); if st == SESSION_CLOSED return (the connection is already closed and its resources are released by the normal teardown). 3. If st == SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT or st == SESSION_READY, call broker_process_input(b, s) once: it frames and handles every complete packet still in the receive buffer, in order, including a final PUBLISH immediately followed by the peer's shutdown, and returns either 0 (only an incomplete tail or nothing remains) or -1 (a frame or handler closed the session). 4. st = session_state(s); if st == SESSION_CLOSED return: the input already closed the connection (DISCONNECT, a malformed final frame or a rejected CONNECT) and its queue was deliberately released, so there is nothing to flush. 5. Discard the partial tail: in = session_input(s); if in is non-NULL and in->len > 0 call buffer_consume(in, in->len). Any bytes that do not form a complete packet can never complete now that the peer stopped sending, and keeping them would make a later teardown copy pointless data. This step is harmless when the buffer already ended on a frame boundary (len == 0). 6. If st != SESSION_CLOSING call session_close_after_flush(s) so the session enters CLOSING with any queued output preserved: the writer pumps the remaining bytes out and only then is the descriptor closed. A session in AWAITING_CONNECT (peer closed before CONNECT) also becomes CLOSING with an empty queue, which broker_reap closes immediately on the next pass.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: void. After the call the session is either SESSION_CLOSED (its input already closed it) or SESSION_CLOSING with its receive buffer emptied and its queued output preserved for the writer; no frames remain buffered, and any final complete PUBLISH has been routed to matching sessions.
INVARIANTS_USED: all complete frames already received are handled before EOF is acted upon
a partial trailing frame is dropped and never interpreted
entering CLOSING never reorders or discards queued output, so a response already produced for this client is flushed first
the descriptor is closed exactly once, by the writer path or by the teardown, never by both
closing one connection leaves other sessions untouched
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: b and s are non-NULL and s is owned by b; the execution layer observed recv returning 0 or a read error on s's descriptor and has not called broker_reap since.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: session_state(s) is SESSION_CLOSED or SESSION_CLOSING; s's receive buffer has len 0; queued output is either empty (input already closed the session) or preserved.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Single-threaded reactor; the session is not accessed concurrently.

EXPECT.note: the publisher is not a subscriber, so it has nothing to flush; its own echo would be flushed if it had matched
the PINGRESP produced by the buffered PINGREQ is written by the writer loop; the descriptor stays open while the queue is nonempty
an unterminated PUBLISH is dropped; no partial packet is ever routed
the DISCONNECT closes immediately, so the EOF path adds nothing and does not resurrect a queue
the complete PINGREQ is answered and only the trailing partial byte is discarded

runtime: subscriber S connects and subscribes 't/#' but sends nothing further
P sends one PUBLISH 't/x' payload 'z' and then shuts down its write side (shutdown(SHUT_WR))

EXPECT.note: S is passive: it never sends extra data to make P's output progress, and P's echo is written while S is idle
